# runr_domain (Resource)

A custom domain of a project. Create the TXT record (`verification_name` / `verification_value`) and the record in `dns_targets` at your DNS provider; the domain serves once it is verified (`verify = true` waits for that, or run `runr domains verify`).

With `environment` the domain routes to one environment of the project, with the DNS targets and certificates of the region the environment runs in. Import with `<project name or id>/<domain>` or `<project name or id>/<environment>/<domain>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "runr_domain" "api" {
  project_id = runr_project.api.id
  domain     = "api.example.com"
  tls_mode   = "cert-manager"
}

# Publish the records at your DNS provider, e.g. with the cloudflare provider:
#   TXT   runr_domain.api.verification_name  = runr_domain.api.verification_value
#   CNAME runr_domain.api.dns_targets[0].name = runr_domain.api.dns_targets[0].value
output "dns_records" {
  value = concat(
    [{ type = runr_domain.api.verification_type, name = runr_domain.api.verification_name, value = runr_domain.api.verification_value }],
    runr_domain.api.dns_targets,
  )
}

# A domain of the staging environment: it routes to staging's workload, with the DNS targets of
# the region staging runs in.
resource "runr_domain" "staging" {
  project_id  = runr_project.api.id
  environment = runr_environment.staging.name
  domain      = "staging.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Host name, e.g. `api.example.com`.
- `project_id` (String) Project id.

### Optional

- `certificate` (String) PEM certificate chain (`tls_mode = "custom"`).
- `environment` (String) Environment the domain routes to (`runr_environment.<name>.name` or its id). Left out (or `production`): the project's own workload. Changing it adds the domain anew.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) PEM private key (`tls_mode = "custom"`).
- `tls_mode` (String) HTTPS certificate: `none` (the region's default certificate, which does not name the domain), `cert-manager` (a certificate for the domain from the region's cert-manager issuer) or `custom`. Left out, RunR chooses when the domain is created — `cert-manager` where the region issues certificates, `none` elsewhere — and the mode the domain has is kept (also one set in the console or with `runr domains tls`).
- `verify` (Boolean) Wait at create until the DNS records are found and the domain is active (default `false`).
- `verify_timeout` (String) How long `verify` waits (Go duration, default `10m`).

### Read-Only

- `dns_targets` (List of Object) Records that route the domain to the project (`type`, `name`, `value`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_targets))
- `id` (String) Domain id.
- `status` (String) `pending`, `verified`, `active` or `error`.
- `url` (String) URL of the domain.
- `verification_name` (String) Ownership record name.
- `verification_type` (String) Ownership record type (`TXT`).
- `verification_value` (String) Ownership record value.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_targets`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String)
- `type` (String)
- `value` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project name or id>/<domain>
terraform import runr_domain.api orders-api/api.example.com

# A domain of an environment: <project name or id>/<environment>/<domain>
terraform import runr_domain.staging orders-api/staging/staging.example.com
```
